meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drink', paired with 'выпивать'.

examples.text: Катя, я могу с тобой выпить?
examples.trans: Katya, may I have a drink with you?

examples.text: Тоже выпить со мной хочешь, да?
examples.trans: You want to have a drink with me too, right?

examples.text: Не знаю, например, выпить с ним чашечку кофе через час.
examples.trans: I do not know, for example, drink a cup of coffee with him in an hour.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это мой ресторан, и я решаю, что здесь едят.
examples.trans: This is my restaurant, and I decide what people eat here.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'Mama' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давай за мою маму и за ее мудрые советы.

examples.text: Давай за мою маму и за ее мудрые советы.
examples.trans: Let's drink to my mom and her wise advice.

meanings.en: nowhere, not anywhere (direction/destination, used with не or нет)
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'nowhere', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ведь ты без них никуда, свободен.

examples.text: Слушайте, да не нужно вам никуда ехать.
examples.trans: Listen, you don't need to go anywhere.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вободный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('free (to go)').

examples.trans: That's all, you can go!
Is this seat free?
That's all, Samson, you can go!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

получаться.gloss: to work out, to come out

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work out, to come out', paired with 'получиться'.

examples.trans: I can't manage it.
Everything is working out!

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right').

examples.text: У нас демократия, один гражданин имеет право нахамить другому.
examples.trans: We have democracy, one citizen has the right to be rude to another.

examples.text: Катя, ты что, правда с ним была?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('at fault, guilty').

обижаться.gloss: to stay offended / hold a grudge

meanings.en: to take offence, to get upset
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ижаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stay offended / hold a grudge', paired with 'обидеться'.

examples.text: Это не повод так долго обижаться.
examples.trans: That is no reason to stay offended for so long.
Don't take offence, Vanya.
Don't be offended by my words.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Я не знаю, я ничего не понял.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not understand anything.

examples.text: Он сказал, что половину слов в меню не понял.
examples.trans: He said that he did not understand half the words on the menu.

examples.text: Я не понял, она у нас работает?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are changing the restaurant's concept.

examples.text: Вы еще меня благодарить будете, когда мы звезду получим.
examples.trans: You will thank me yet when we get the star.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'works', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.trans: I agree to work for you.

examples.text: Я не понял, она у нас работает?
examples.trans: I do not understand, does she work here with us?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Но это у нас, а тут другая страна.
examples.trans: But that is back home, and here is another country.
